rationale: The three blunt-force injury types (abrasion, contusion, laceration) are core FM5.1 recall. Placing after block 4 (blunt force content) tests the critical definitional distinctions before students encounter sharp force injuries.
The stab-versus-incised wound dimensional rule (depth > length vs length > depth) is a frequently tested factual distinction. Placed after the sharp force injuries block for immediate consolidation.

BNS Section 118 lists exactly 8 categories of grievous hurt — a high-yield fact under FM5.2. Placed after the BNS definitions block so students can immediately test recall of the statutory categories.
Ante-mortem vs post-mortem injury distinction via vital reaction is a critical FM5.3 skill. Placed after the vital reaction content block to test the conceptual basis immediately.

The four phases of wound healing (haemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, remodelling) and their approximate timelines are core FM5.4 content. This question tests one specific timeline fact that students often misremember.
Determining cause of death in wound cases (primary vs secondary/proximate cause) is the applied skill under FM5.5. This question tests clinical application of the causal chain principle.

Weapon classification into blunt/sharp-edged/sharp-pointed/combined is a foundational FM5.6 fact. Placed after the classification content block to test recall before the more detailed named-weapon section.
Weapon examination procedure and chain of custody are the applied skills under FM14.10. This question tests whether students understand the documentation obligation when examining a submitted weapon.

The structured 8-step MLC examination protocol is core FM14.1 applied practice. Placed after the examination procedure content block; tests recall of the mandatory first step (consent) before students reach the report-writing section.

FM14.9 requires identifying medicolegal specimens and inferring their significance. Placed after the applied MLC practice block to test integration of examination findings into a complete report opinion.
